title: Saltmarsh retail checkout LLM field notes
content:
Context:
- Saltmarsh (regional grocery chain) exploring LLM assistant at checkout: customer-facing clarifications + operator quick-help for register attendants. Pilot scope: 5 stores, 2 registers each, peak concurrency ~12 sessions, avg session length 40–120s.

Call notes (2024-10-18, 30m sync):
- Attendees: Anna Lopez (Saltmarsh product), Marcus Chen (ops), Jordan Kim, Samira Patel.
- They want natural-language clarifications for discounts, coupon edge-cases, returns policy during checkout and a short operator prompt generator for manual overrides.
- Hard constraints: cannot send PANs or CVV to any external API; tokenization needed. Also must retain logs for 90 days for disputes (redaction required).
- Ops question: can we run in their VPC? Yes — Private deployment preferred, Dedicated capacity discussed as fallback for SLA.

Initial technical requirements / quick draft:
- Minimum throughput: handle bursts up to 20 req/s for pilot region (safety headroom).
- Latency SLO: <200ms p50 for short clarifications, <600ms p95. If hosted cannot meet p95, propose in-region dedicated.
- Model: small-to-medium conversational model with streaming answer support and explicit sensitive-field filters.
- Data flow: POS -> saltmarsh middleware (on-prem) -> Redwood Private ingress (via VPC peering) -> inference. Middleware strips/obfuscates PANs and attaches order context id only.
- Audit log: redact PII at ingestion; store request hashes + deterministic prompt mapping for dispute replays.

Prompt examples (raw, for internal eval):
- "Customer says they have a buy-one-get-one coupon but barcode doesn't scan. What to say?"
- "Customer returns item purchased 35 days ago, no receipt. Outline return policy and escalation steps."

Gotchas / risks uncovered:
- PCI scope creep: even truncated card last4 sometimes flagged in logs; need explicit sanitizer tests (unit + e2e).
- Sequence length: context can contain 6–10 line items (~1.2k tokens) — recommend prefix caching and compact item summaries before sending to model.
- Cost: naive calls for every small clarification will inflate tokens; add a local rule engine to short-circuit trivial questions (e.g., price/qty lookups).
- Offline mode: registers must function if network drops — local fallback responses (static FAQ) required.
- Operator UX: streaming partial answers ok, but need final-answer confirmation step before applying overrides.

Preliminary infra advice:
- Start on Redwood Private in their primary cloud region to avoid cross-region egress and latency.
- Use Dedicated reserved pool for pilot hours (9am–9pm local), autoscale to burst policy for weekends.
- Enable prefix caching for repetitive product lookup prompts; keep TTL 30m, invalidate on price updates.
- Quantization: q4f16 or similar for smaller model to hit latency targets on A100/RTX cluster.

Metrics to capture in pilot:
- Mean token usage per session
- Model latency p50/p95/p99
- % queries answered by local rule-engine vs model
- Escalation rate to human attendant
- Cost per session (estimate)

Open questions / ACTIONS:
- [Anna] Confirm exact list of fields we are allowed to send (PII gating) — due 2024-10-25.
- [Samira] Put together cost estimate: hosted vs private vs dedicated for pilot (ballpark) — due 2024-10-21.
- [Jordan] Draft sample sanitizer library (JS middleware) and unit tests for redaction patterns — initial PR by 2024-10-24.
- [Ethan] Run quick latency sim using a small distil-chat model to validate <200ms p50 on dedicated instance — report 2024-10-22.
- Engineering question: can we support token-level billing + per-route quotas for pilot? (Use for chargeback with Saltmarsh)

Notes to self / rough next steps:
- Build minimal demo: product-summary -> obfuscation -> 1-shot prompt template -> model response. Keep examples short.
- Prepare runbook snippet for register attendants (how to escalate, privacy reminders).
- Add checklist for PCI acceptance: signed DPA + architecture review + sanitizer tests before any live data.

Misc scribbles:
- Consider using embeddings for product SKU fuzzy-match before constructing full prompt (saves tokens).
- Potential quick win: local rules for coupon verification (if coupon code matches pattern X and within date range, auto-approve)

Status: draft — heavy engineering coordination needed. Will iterate after answers from Anna + latency sim results.
